findings.expected: After three runs in a row with nothing merged the task is disabled, whatever those runs left on GitHub (the TOLD column), and the rule can be decided from data the session has.
findings.how_it_arises: This is a model of the rule text: no code implements the rule, a session decides it from what the GitHub tools return. H3/H4: a failure before step 6 that has a standing cause repeats every week; no pull request is ever opened, so "the three most recent ones" never exist and the task neither stops nor says so. H2: one comment from the owner exempts a pull request, so a fourth is opened. H7: an owner who answers in the chat and merges the built proposals, not the report pull requests, gets a working loop switched off. H1: the session acts on GitHub under the owner's login (the merge of PR #34, made by the session's merge tool, is recorded with the owner as author), so "untouched by the owner" cannot be read from GitHub's author fields and the session has to guess. Separately, when the stop path is followed exactly as stored (plan-gate, update_trigger, end) the Stop gate blocks the end of the run once, because adversarial-verify is ordered only "before step 6" (bb_cases.py B05: block:F1 on all three hook sets).
